entities.summary:
Pherecydes of Leros (pherecydes-of-leros) was an ancient Greek historian who authored three significant works: On Leros, On Iphigenia, and On the Festivals of Dionysus. 

    Born in the 5th or 6th century BCE, Pherecydes lived 'before the seventy-fifth Olympiad,' a period spanning approximately 550-480 BCE. His writings provide valuable insights into the cultural and historical context of ancient Greece during this time.

    As a historian, Pherecydes' most notable contribution was his meticulous recording of the island of Leros' history, which included its early settlements, notable figures, and cultural practices. His works also touched upon other aspects of ancient Greek life, such as the myths of Iphigenia and the festivals of Dionysus.

    Pherecydes' significance extends beyond his individual works, as they offer a unique window into the cultural and historical landscape of ancient Greece. His writings have been preserved in various ancient sources, including the Suda, and continue to provide valuable information for historians and scholars today.

    The legacy of Pherecydes can be seen in the continued study and analysis of his works, which have contributed to a deeper understanding of ancient Greek history and culture. His contributions have had a lasting impact on the field of classical studies, and his works remain an essential part of the historical record.

    One striking aspect of Pherecydes' life and work is the scarcity of information about his personal life. Despite his importance as a historian, very little is known about his birth, death, or personal relationships. This lack of information only adds to the enigma surrounding Pherecydes, making him all the more fascinating and intriguing to scholars and historians.
